build.summary: V32 is done on branch research/production-loop-20261116-w4-v32 (head b9bbd934, not pushed). Only run_concurrency_probe changed in stage_batch.rs, plus the OnceLock import. Each probe task marks itself active, then sleeps in 100 us steps until two tasks have been active at once or a shared deadline (first task's arrival + 2 s) passes. The checksum composition, report schema, 8 tasks x 1 ms and 4-thread pool are unchanged. stage_batch.rs blob c2f44c32 -> fb68321b; the orchestrator must re-pin it (OD-L1-28). Old failure: the task-text strace runs (1 and 2 CPUs) gave 0/160. strace with busy loops on the tracer's CPU gave 6/680, each with the hosted checksum 577161eb. The late-worker test (a global allocator delays rayon workers with index >= 1 by 300 ms) fails on the old probe 20/20 and passes on the new one 20/20. New CLI: 0/400 runs false, all 4079849b. Interleaved busy-loop runs: old 4/240 vs new 0/240. Diagnostic: longest rendezvous wait 33 ms, against the 2 s bound. cli_contracts, the stage_batch tests, clippy and fmt pass. The loop checker flags only the stage_batch.rs blob.

Task-text conditions (strace -f on 1/2 CPUs) did not provoke the failure (0/160). Provocation needed busy loops on the tracer's CPU, and its rate is low, so the CLI comparison is statistically weak. The deterministic evidence is the late-worker test.

provoke.sh defect kept and documented: the kill reaches only the wrapper subshell, so 30 s busy loops accumulated on CPU 8 (tens alive, rebuilt from runs.tsv). It affected old and new runs alike in b2.
Hosted tracing mode (strace -ff --seccomp-bpf -e trace=<file syscalls>) was not reproduced exactly; strace -f -e trace=none was used
Residual by design: a host on which no second worker runs within 2 s still reports parallel-observed=false (the 2 s wait is paid once per report)
The late-worker test relies on rayon-core 1.13 and crossbeam-epoch, where a worker's first allocation comes at its first steal; a late>=3 guard checks that the delay fired
New ignored diagnostic test stage_batch_probe_latency copies the probe's structure; it must be kept in step if the probe's constants change

rulings: An integration test cannot reach the private probe pool. The 'workers delayed' test therefore uses a test-binary global allocator that delays rayon workers with index >= 1 at their first allocation, so stage_batch.rs gets no test hook.

The pinned checksum 4079849b is asserted only when every row's max_abs_difference is exactly 0 (true on this host and the hosted runner). The composition is checked on every host, so no new host-dependent bit anchor is added.

The task-text strace runs did not provoke the failure, so conditions were added: busy loops, a shared tracer and a no-strace control. All are labelled as additions. Old and new runs were interleaved in b2.
The provoke.sh busy-loop defect was documented and quantified, not fixed and rerun, so the committed script is the one that produced the logs
Raw reports are packed per condition into reports.tar.xz with a sha256 manifest, verified by read-back
Wall times and rendezvous waits are labelled diagnostic and no verdict uses them
